recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No CodeSystem follow-up is needed for FHIR-16718; any reassessment of separate ValueSet or ConceptMap CTS2 wording should be handled under its own issue.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification vocab issue FHIR-16718 asked that the CodeSystem Boundaries and Relationships text stop implying a direct OMG CTS 2 conversion path and instead clarify that the CodeSystem design is based only in part on CTS 2 code-system functionality and can be published from CTS2-maintained code systems.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in svn revision 14684, now Git commit 796eaa733e83bb1d9e30738e106152b7415c32df, which changed source/codesystem/codesystem-introduction.xml from the old OMG CTS 2 conversion wording to the current partial-basis wording. The applied commit used the clearer phrase "A CTS2 server can be used to maintain code systems which are then published using the CodeSystem resource," rather than the Jira resolution's apparent "CTS2 code system" wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has an active codesystem=CodeSystem resource entry, so source/codesystem/codesystem-introduction.xml is in current build scope. Current source still contains the applied text at lines 73-75 and a source-wide search found no remaining CodeSystem text saying CodeSystem resources can be converted to CTS2. Jira search surfaced FHIR-5479 as older ValueSet/Core Principles background, but it concerns ValueSet wording and is not a CodeSystem follow-up. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant or conflicting community discussion for FHIR-16718.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active CodeSystem source already reflects the applied FHIR-16718 decision and avoids the misleading direct-conversion claim.

related_jiras.note: Surfaced in a CTS2 Jira search, but it is an older ValueSet clarification and does not change the CodeSystem reconciliation.
